issue.author: krassowski
issue.body_normalized:
### Problem

- CodeMirror does not implement block comment for Python language which means executing block comment shortcut is no-op in Python and users think it is broken
- Python does not define block comment syntax, although `"""` is _de facto_ standard substitute as blessed by BDFL
- we want to keep separate block and line comments shortcuts for users using languages which do have as separate block comments

### Proposed Solution

Either or both:
- (a) use `pythonLanguage.data.of({commentTokens: ...})` to add `"""` as block comment for Python - this only helps for Python
- (b) replace uses of `toggleBlockComment` with a composite command which tries to run `toggleBlockComment` first and `toggleComment` second if the former did not succeed (or check if language data have `commentTokens.block` defined)

### Additional context

See discussion in upstream issue https://github.com/codemirror/dev/issues/1372 - upstream will not include that command nor the `"""` syntax for Python so it is up to JupyterLab to implement it.

pull_request.author: altis0725
pull_request.body_normalized:
## References

Fixes #16212

Related: #16770 (earlier attempt, stale)

## Code changes

Add a composite command `toggleBlockCommentOrFallback` in `packages/codemirror/src/commands.ts` that:
1. Tries `toggleBlockComment(view)` first
2. Falls back to `toggleComment(view)` when the language (e.g. Python) does not define block comment tokens in CodeMirror

The keybinding for `toggle-block-comment` is updated to use this composite command.

## User-facing changes

Languages like Python that lack block comment syntax will now toggle line comments (`#`) when the block comment shortcut (Alt+A / Alt+A) is pressed, instead of silently doing nothing.

## Backwards-incompatible changes

None. The shortcut previously was a no-op for languages without block comments; it now falls back to line comments.
